intended_object: The off-diagonal of a finite set s, i.e. the finite set {(a, b) ∈ s × s | a ≠ b}. This comes from the docstring.
explanation: The definition works on the underlying list of the finset, which has no duplicates. `List.offDiag l` pairs each element x, at index n, with every element of `l.eraseIdx n`, i.e. the list with x's position removed. Because the list has no duplicates, this produces exactly the pairs (x, y) with x and y in l and x ≠ y. The construction respects permutations (`List.Perm.offDiag`) and the result has no duplicates (`hs.offDiag`), so it gives a well-defined Finset. The lemma `Finset.mem_offDiag` confirms that x ∈ s.offDiag ↔ x.1 ∈ s ∧ x.2 ∈ s ∧ x.1 ≠ x.2, which matches `Set.offDiag` and the docstring. The definition works for any type α and does not even require `DecidableEq`, so it is at its natural generality. It is the finset version of `Set.offDiag`.
